name: diff
summary: Compares two files line by line.
description: Shows the differences between two files, or between two directories with -r. The unified format (-u) is the most readable: lines prefixed with - come from the first file, those prefixed with + from the second, and @@ shows the position. It is the format of patches and of git diff. The exit code is 0 if the files are identical and 1 if they differ.

options.description: Unified format, with 3 lines of context around each difference.
Shows the two files side by side.
Only reports whether the files differ, without details.
Ignores blank lines that were added or removed.
With -r, treats a file missing on one side as an empty file.

arguments.name: FILE2
arguments.description: File (or directory) to compare, the “new” one.

examples.explanation: Lists the files that differ between two versions of a project.
Saves the differences to a patch file, which can be applied with patch.
